title: Expanded Hom bijections and counit for finite closed site transport
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $S_T=\nu_T^*$ and $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$ for the comparison adjunction, and denote its counit by $e_T:S_TU_T\to1$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $F=i_{\mathrm{et},*}$ be exact termwise derived direct image, identify $Ri_!^c=F$ for $c=(\operatorname{id}_Z,i)$ by [lem-pur-closed-unbounded-compact-support-normalization], and write $G=i_c^\times$ for its ordinary etale right adjoint with counit $\epsilon^G:FG\to1$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Pro-etale direct image on module sheaves is exact, and its total unbounded right derived functor is canonically its termwise descent $P=i_{\mathrm{proet},*}$. For $H\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the canonical direct-image comparison of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] is a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_H:S_XFH\xrightarrow{\sim}PS_ZH.$$
Under the identity-extension identifications, the compact-support comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] at the identity etale-origin witness is exactly $\lambda_H^{-1}$.

Let $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and assume $E_L=GU_XL\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The finite transported exceptional value is $Ri^!L=S_ZE_L$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For every $H\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, its transported relative adjunction is the specified composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}(PS_ZH,L)\xrightarrow{f\mapsto f\circ\lambda_H}\operatorname{Hom}(S_XFH,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FH,U_XL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,GU_XL)\xrightarrow{S_Z}\operatorname{Hom}(S_ZH,S_ZGU_XL),$$
where the middle bijections are the comparison adjunction and $F\dashv G$, and the last is comparison full faithfulness on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. The inverse image of $1_{S_ZE_L}$ under this bijection is the transported exceptional counit, and it equals
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{tr}}_L=e_{X,L}\circ S_X(\epsilon^G_{U_XL})\circ\lambda_{E_L}^{-1}:PS_ZE_L\longrightarrow L.$$
The formula is natural on the full subcategory of such $L$. It asserts only this relative adjunction, not an adjunction on all unbounded pro-etale inputs.

source.place: Displayed finite transported Hom chain, specialized to the first closed localization triangle of sk-prop-a1; expanded inverse image of the identity (returned item Step 5).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a) and [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $i$ is proper and qcqs, so $c=(\operatorname{id}_Z,i)$ is an allowed compactification. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], choose $d\geq0$ with $\dim Z\leq d$ (take $d=0$ for $Z=\varnothing$). The etale normalization [lem-pur-closed-unbounded-compact-support-normalization] gives $Ri_!^c=F$ and shows that $FH$ is bounded below whenever $H$ is. By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], the quasi-compact complement in the hypotheses makes pro-etale module direct image exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to this exact functor: its termwise descent $P$ exists on the whole unbounded category, and the canonical map from termwise direct image to total right derived direct image is invertible on every complex. Thus $Ri_{\mathrm{proet},*}=P$ with the specified canonical identification.

source.place: Finite-coefficient and compactification hypotheses before the displayed Hom chain; Stacks 01W5, 01W1 and 015F (derived.tex, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor).

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] to $i$ and $H\in D^+$; Step 1 verifies qcqs. Under the exact-derived identifications this gives the natural isomorphism $\lambda_H:S_XFH\to PS_ZH$. It is the named canonical direct-image mate of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Apply [lem-coef-proper-identity-open-site-comparison] with $f=i$ and its etale input $H$. Its equation $S_X(e_H)C_{c,H}q_{S_ZH}^{-1}=b_{i,H}^{-1}$ identifies the compact-support comparison with $\lambda_H^{-1}$ after removing identity extension by zero. Its final assertion verifies that the identity-open comparison contributes the identity, so no extra automorphism is inserted.

source.place: Compact-support factor of the Hom chain; identity-open normalization of the preceding compact-support comparison.

proof.text: For $L$ as in the statement put $E=GU_XL$. By hypothesis $E\in D^+$, and [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] gives $S_ZE,S_ZH\in D^+$. The formula [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] identifies the exceptional value with $S_ZE$. Apply [lem-coef-relative-hom-change-of-presentation] with $f=i$, etale input $H$, pro-etale target $M=L$, and the exact-derived presentations $F,P$ from Step 1. Use the induced adjunction $F\dashv G$; after this identification its adjoint-conjugation map is the identity. Its dimension hypothesis is Step 1, and its two lower-bound hypotheses are $FH\in D^+$ and $GU_XL=E\in D^+$. Step 2 makes its $B_H=\lambda_H$. Its equality therefore gives precisely the specified four-factor Hom map in the item. The first map is bijective since $\lambda_H$ is invertible, the middle maps are the specified adjunction bijections, and the last is bijective by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] applied to the two bounded-below etale objects $H,E$. In particular this conclusion does not require $L$ to be of etale origin.

source.place: The four arrows of the displayed finite transported Hom chain, on their bounded-below domains.

proof.text:
Set $H=E$. Reverse the four bijections of Step 3 on $1_{S_ZE}$. The inverse fully faithful Hom map sends it to $1_E$, since functors preserve identities. For $F\dashv G$, [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] sends $1_E$ backwards to $\epsilon^G_{U_XL}:FE\to U_XL$. Applying the same lemma to $S_X\dashv U_X$ sends this backwards to $e_{X,L}\circ S_X(\epsilon^G_{U_XL}):S_XFE\to L$. Finally inverse precomposition by $\lambda_E$ gives
$$t_L=e_{X,L}\circ S_X(\epsilon^G_{U_XL})\circ\lambda_E^{-1}:PS_ZE\to L.$$
Each reversal is of the specified bijection, so $t_L$ is its unique inverse image of the identity, exactly the relative exceptional counit in the statement.

source.place: Inverse image of the identity in the four-factor display; Stacks categories.tex, Definition 0037 and the following unit/counit formulas.

proof.text: For a morphism $u:L\to L'$ between allowed targets, put $v=GU_X(u):E_L\to E_{L'}$. Naturality of the etale counit gives $\epsilon^G_{U_XL'}\circ F(v)=U_X(u)\circ\epsilon^G_{U_XL}$. Naturality of $\lambda^{-1}$ gives $\lambda_{E_{L'}}^{-1}\circ PS_Z(v)=S_XF(v)\circ\lambda_{E_L}^{-1}$, and naturality of the comparison counit gives $e_{X,L'}\circ S_XU_X(u)=u\circ e_{X,L}$. Substitution in Step 4 yields $t_{L'}\circ PS_Z(v)=u\circ t_L$. These are the required naturality squares. All maps lie in the full subcategory specified by $L,E_L\in D^+$; the argument asserts no exceptional adjunction outside it.
